subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should ordered agent bootstrap hook handlers remain one uninterrupted shared-context mutation chain, or may unrelated event-loop callbacks interleave between handlers?
rationale: Both approaches preserve handler order, but inter-handler yielding changes when partially transformed bootstrap context can coexist with unrelated runtime work; current documentation and tests do not define that contract.

options.title: Retain uninterrupted dispatch
options.body: Remove the inter-handler setImmediate while preserving asynchronous workspace reads, cooperative glob traversal, timing diagnostics, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Approve cooperative interleaving
options.body: Keep the yield and add explicit tests for reentrant bootstrap activity and visibility of shared-event mutations between handlers.

options.title: Split the uncontroversial fix
options.body: Land the workspace I/O, glob, and timing changes separately if the hook scheduling decision cannot be resolved promptly.

recommendation.title: Retain uninterrupted dispatch
recommendation.body: Remove the inter-handler setImmediate while preserving asynchronous workspace reads, cooperative glob traversal, timing diagnostics, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced both the internal hook system and the bootstrap hook boundary whose scheduling contract is being changed.
